newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech finmin sends market watchdog plan to cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Czech finmin sends market watchdog plan to cabinet.

text.p: The Czech finance ministry sent a draft proposal to create an independent securities commission to the government on Friday, a plan which would end the ministry's job as watchdog for the capital markets.
In a statement, ministry spokeswoman Ludmila Nutilova said the plan for the new commission had been signed by Finance Minister Ivan Pilip and sent to the government for approval.
It would then need to be ratified in parliament.

"(The plan) suggests to set up a separate subject for the performance of supervision over the capital market whilch would take over the supervisory powers from the ministry of finance," Nutilova said.
"(The plan) concerns the resolution of the status of state supervision such as is normal in the world," the statement added.

The finance ministry has faced stiff criticism from many investors who say its lax enforcement of securities regulations have left the Czech capital markets rife with insider trading and dubious transactions.

Many market participants, including Prague Stock Exchange chairman Tomas Jezek, have called on the government to set up an independent watchdog akin to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).
In a government programme announced in April, the cabinet directed the finance ministry to draft legislation by May 31 to set up an independent securities commission.
Details of the proposal signed on Friday have yet to be released.
